chapterNote: A psalm with a crime scene in its title. Doeg the Edomite watched David take bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech the priest, went to Saul, and told — and eighty-five priests died for it, with their town put to the sword (1 Samuel 22). David's answer is not a lament but an interrogation of the informer: why do you boast in evil, mighty man? The covenant love of God lasts all day long — longer than your influence. Your tongue plots ruin like a sharpened razor; you love evil more than good, lying more than righteous speech, every word that swallows people whole. Then the verdict, in four verbs: God will pull you down, snatch you up, tear you out of your tent, and uproot you from the land of the living. The righteous will watch, and fear, and laugh — the laughter of Psalm 2, not of cruelty — and say: there is the man who would not make God his stronghold. And against the uprooted tent David sets himself: I am like a green olive tree in the house of God, trusting in His covenant love forever and ever. Uprooted informer, planted worshiper; the psalm is one long contrast between what a tongue can do and what God's chesed outlasts.

1.text: For the choir director. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, 'David has come to the house of Ahimelech.' Why do you boast in evil, mighty man? The covenant love of God lasts all day long.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], Maschil [maskil], A Psalm of David, when Doeg the Edomite came [bo] and told [nagad] Saul, and said [amar] unto him, David is come [bo] to the house [bayith] of Ahimelech. Why boast [halal] you yourself in mischief [ra — evil], O mighty [gibbor] man? the goodness [chesed — covenant love] of God [El] endures continually [yom — all the day].
1.notes: The longest title in Book Two, and it names a real informer: Doeg the Edomite (H1673, H130), Saul's chief herdsman, who saw David at Nob and reported it — and then killed eighty-five priests when Saul's own guard would not (1 Samuel 22:9-19). mah-tithallel be-raah ha-gibbor (H1984, H7451, H1368): why do you BOAST in evil, gibbor — 'mighty man', said to a man whose might was informing; chesed El kol-ha-yom (H2617, H410, H3117): the chesed of God is all the day long. One line, and the contest is set: a man's moment against God's covenant love, which outlasts the news cycle.

2.text: Your tongue devises ruin, like a sharpened razor, worker of deceit.
2.amp: Your tongue [lashon] devises [chashab] mischiefs [havvah — ruin]; like a sharp razor, working [asah] deceitfully [remiyah].
2.notes: havvot tachshob leshonekha (H1942, H2803, H3956): your tongue RECKONS UP ruin — chashab, the accountant's verb, evil worked out carefully; ke-taar melutash oseh remiyah (H8593, H3913, H6213, H7423): like a whetted razor, working remiyah, treachery. A razor is a grooming tool that happens to be a weapon: the informer told the truth, and the truth cut throats.

3.text: Evil you have loved more than good, and falsehood more than righteous speech. Selah.
3.amp: You love [ahab] evil [ra] more than good [tov]; and lying [sheqer] rather than to speak [dabar] righteousness [tsedek]. Selah [Selah].
3.notes: ahabta ra mi-tov (H157, H7451, H2896): you have LOVED evil more than good — love, not weakness: the psalm's charge is about affections, not lapses; sheqer mi-dabber tsedek (H8267, H1696, H6664): falsehood more than speaking righteousness. Selah. Doeg's report was factually accurate, which is why the charge is sheqer at the level of the heart, not of the sentence.

4.text: You love every devouring word, O deceitful tongue.
4.amp: You love [ahab] all devouring [bala — swallowing] words [dabar], O ['and the deceitful tongue', mirmah, the KJV margin] you deceitful [mirmah] tongue [lashon].
4.notes: ahabta khol-dibre-bala (H157, H1697, H1105): you love all words that SWALLOW — bala, the verb for the earth opening on Korah (Numbers 16:32) and the sea on Egypt (Exodus 15:12): speech that makes people disappear; leshon mirmah (H3956, H4820): tongue of deceit. James 3:6 on the tongue as a fire is the New Testament's version of this verse.

5.text: God Himself will pull you down forever; He will snatch you up and tear you from your tent, and uproot you out of the land of the living. Selah.
5.amp: God [El] shall likewise destroy ['beat thee down', nathats, the KJV margin] you for ever [netsach], He shall take you away [chathah — snatch, as coals], and pluck you out of your dwelling place [ohel — tent], and root you out of the land [eretz] of the living [chay]. Selah [Selah].
5.notes: gam-El yittotskha la-netsach (H410, H5422, H5331): God Himself will PULL YOU DOWN — the margin's 'beat thee down', the verb for demolishing an altar — forever. yachtekha ve-yissachakha me-ohel (H2846, H5255, H168): He will SNATCH you — chathah, the word for scooping live coals off a hearth (Isaiah 30:14) — and tear you from your tent. ve-shereshkha me-erets chayyim (H8327, H776, H2416): and uproot you from the land of the living. Four verbs of demolition against the man who demolished a priestly town; and the last of them, root, sets up verse 8's tree.

6.text: The righteous will see and be afraid, and they will laugh at him:
6.amp: The righteous [tsaddiq] also shall see [raah], and fear [yare], and shall laugh [sachaq] at him:
6.notes: ve-yiru tsaddiqim ve-yirau (H7200, H6662, H3372): the righteous will SEE and FEAR — a near-pun in Hebrew, and the right order: they are frightened before they are amused. ve-alav yischaqu (H7832): and at him they will LAUGH — the laughter of Psalm 2:4, where God laughs at the kings: not cruelty but the collapse of a bluff (cf. Job 22:19).

7.text: 'Look — the man who would not make God his stronghold, who trusted in his great wealth and made himself strong in his own ruin!'
7.amp: Lo, this is the man [geber] that made [sum] not God [Elohim] his strength [maoz — stronghold]; but trusted [batach] in the abundance [rob] of his riches, and strengthened [azaz] himself in his wickedness ['substance', havvah, the KJV margin].
7.notes: hinneh ha-geber lo yasim Elohim mauzzo (H1397, H7760, H430, H4581): LOOK — the geber, the strong man of verse 1, who would not make God his maoz, his stronghold. va-yibtach be-rob oshro (H982, H7230): he trusted in the abundance of his riches. yaoz be-havvato (H5810, H1942): he made himself strong in his havvah — his ruin, or, the margin's reading, his substance: the word is the same one his tongue was devising in verse 2. A man made strong by the very thing that destroys him.

8.text: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the covenant love of God forever and ever.
8.amp: But I am like a green olive tree [zayith] in the house [bayith] of God [Elohim]: I trust [batach] in the mercy [chesed — covenant love] of God [Elohim] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
8.notes: va-ani ke-zayit raanan be-bet Elohim (H2132, H7488, H1004, H430): but I am like a LEAFY olive tree in the house of God — raanan, green and thriving; the olive is the long-lived tree of the land, and this one is planted indoors, in the courts (cf. Psalm 92:13). batachti be-chesed-Elohim olam va-ed (H982, H2617, H5769, H5703): I have TRUSTED in the chesed of God forever and ever — the same trust Doeg put in his riches (v. 7), aimed somewhere that lasts. Uprooted informer, planted worshiper.

9.text: I will thank You forever, because You have done it; and I will wait on Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your faithful ones.
9.amp: I will praise [yadah — thank] You for ever [olam], because You have done [asah] it: and I will wait [qavah] on Your name [shem]; for it is good [tov] before Your saints [chasid — covenant-loyal ones].
9.notes: odekha le-olam ki asita (H3034, H5769, H6213): I will thank You forever, because YOU have done it — 'it' unnamed: the whole reversal of verses 5-8. va-aqavveh shimkha ki-tov (H6960, H8034, H2896): and I will WAIT on Your name, for it is good — qavah, the taut cord of Psalm 39:7. neged chasidekha (H5048, H2623): in front of Your chasidim, Your covenant-loyal ones — the very company Doeg butchered at Nob, gathered again and listening.
